title: Pauri 22, sound: paataalaa paataal

cards: Stand in an elevator in a very tall building and look at the buttons. Basement, sub-basement, parking level three. Above you, floor after floor, up to a number you can barely read.
Now imagine the buttons never end, in either direction. Below the lowest basement, another. Above the top floor, another sky.
Yesterday Japji asked when. Today it asks where, and how far, and the first line of Pauri 22 sounds like that endless elevator.

teach.b: Here's the line, in the original: paataalaa paataal lakh aagaasaa aagaas. Take it apart. Paataal, paa-TAAL: the lower worlds, the regions under the earth.
Old Indian cosmology spoke of many of them, one below another. So paataalaa paataal: underworlds below underworlds.
Lakh: a hundred thousand, the word Indians still use for big numbers, as in five lakh rupees. Aagaas, aa-GAAS: sky, the heavens, related to the Sanskrit akasha.
Aagaasaa aagaas: skies beyond skies. Put together: underworlds below underworlds, and hundreds of thousands of skies above skies. Now listen to the build.
Each half doubles its word. The first form, with the extra aa, reaches; the second lands. It sounds like going down a staircase, step after step, then climbing into the sky, step after step.
The line doesn't describe the size of the universe. It lets the mouth do the measuring. It also carries on what the countless stanzas started, now with a direction.
This is depth and height: down, down, up, up.
The rest of the stanza asks whether anyone has found the end, and whether it could ever be written. That's tomorrow. Today, just the elevator, and its sound.

how: Pauri 22 is recited in the morning Japji Sahib; its opening line, with its doubled words, has a rhythm that can be heard even before the meaning.

games.q: you're in an elevator that goes down forever and up forever. which line of Japji are you living?
games.why: underworlds below underworlds, hundreds of thousands of skies above skies: Pauri 22's opening.

practice: Say the line aloud: paataalaa paataal, lakh aagaasaa aagaas. On the first half, let your attention sink into your seat, the floor, the ground beneath; on the second, let it rise to the crown of your head and the space above it.
Say it twice more, then sit quietly between the two, the ground below and the open space above.

wordCard.voice: Paataal, the lower worlds beneath the earth. It opens paataalaa paataal, lakh aagaasaa aagaas: underworlds below underworlds, hundreds of thousands of skies above skies.

orig.note: Gurmukhi, Japji Pauri 22, line 1: underworlds below underworlds, a hundred thousand skies above skies.

carryVoice: Your line: paataalaa paataal. Down without a bottom, up without a top. See you tomorrow.
